Which strike trees the fire-weather winds would throw into the line

Source: R/wind.R
wind_fall_exposure.Rd

For each potential strike tree from assess_risk(), works out the arc of fall directions that reach a conductor, then the share of fire-weather hours whose wind would push the tree into that arc.

Usage

wind_fall_exposure(
  risk,
  profile,
  wind_hours,
  phase_offset_m = 3,
  growth_m = 0,
  spread_deg = 15,
  windward_min = 0.5,
  min_hours = 24
)

Arguments

risk

Output of assess_risk().

profile

Output of conductor_profile() (line geometry).

wind_hours

Output of fire_wind_hours().

phase_offset_m, growth_m

As used in assess_risk().

spread_deg

Allowance (degrees, each side) for fall directions that deviate from the wind direction.

windward_min

Share of fire-weather hours at or above which a strike tree counts as windward of the line.

min_hours

Fewer fire-weather hours than this gives a warning: the hit shares then rest on a handful of hours. With none at all, every wind column is NA, not zero.

Value

risk with added tree columns bearing_deg (grid bearing from the tree to the line), arc_lo_deg, arc_hi_deg (half-width of the hitting arc under each conductor bound; NA when it cannot reach), wind_hit_lo, wind_hit_hi (share of fire-weather hours that would throw it into the line), and segment columns wind_strike_lo, wind_strike_hi (sum of wind_hit_* over strike trees: the expected number thrown towards the line in a fire-weather hour), n_strike_windward_lo, n_strike_windward_hi and n_fire_weather_hours (so the hour count survives st_write()). The fire-wind summary is stored in attr(risk$segments, "wind").

Details

A tree of height h whose base is a horizontal distance d from the outer phase, with the conductor dz above its base, reaches the conductor horizontally out to R = sqrt(h^2 - dz^2). It hits if it falls within acos(d / R) of the direction straight at the line, the same 3D test as the fall-in screen, resolved by direction. Windthrown trees fall roughly downwind, so a fire-weather hour counts against the tree when the direction the wind blows towards lies inside that arc, widened by spread_deg on each side for the scatter of real fall directions.

Wind directions are rotated from true north to grid north (meridian convergence at the corridor) before they are compared with tree bearings.
